close_reason: Implemented Jidoka-owned constrained environments across ordered automation cells, with CLI public-data integration and lifecycle tests.
description:
## Outcome

A matrix cell with a resolved profile uses one Jidoka-owned execution environment across its ordered turns. Cancellation, error, hibernation, recovery, and completion follow the lifecycle contract.

## Why now

All contracts now exist. This story connects them without moving provider work into the CLI.

## Current state

Plan places arbitrary `runtime_opts` on a cell. The engine starts a Jidoka session and runs the sequence. No environment is opened, acquired, checkpointed, restored, closed, or cleaned. A cell already has the correct isolation unit: one fresh session and ordered turns.

## Ownership and boundary

Both repositories change. Jidoka attaches the resolved environment to the session sequence and effects. The CLI passes public resolved data and maps the public terminal outcome. Third-party execution remains behind the Jidoka port. The CLI does not import an adapter.

## Detailed implementation

1. In Jidoka, let a sequence accept a resolved execution-environment registration and policy request through public runtime options.
2. Open or restore before the first protected effect, acquire for active work, and make the environment capability available only through runtime context.
3. Checkpoint at the documented session/effect safe points. Use the same binding across ordered turns in one cell.
4. Close after each terminal active use. Apply the trusted retention rule: ephemeral cells cleanup after complete, error, or cancellation; hibernated/recoverable cells retain a checkpoint; durable cells cleanup only through an explicit trusted action.
5. In the CLI engine, pass the resolved profile data. Do not call lifecycle callbacks or carry a handle.
6. Map lifecycle rejection, open failure, evidence failure, cleanup failure, and cancellation to stable execution outcomes.
7. A cell without a profile continues to run without an environment and reports `not_requested` later.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One profiled cell opens at most one durable environment and shares it only across its own turns.
- [ ] Different cells never share a binding unless a future explicit pool contract allows it.
- [ ] The first protected effect cannot run before acquire and evidence validation.
- [ ] Cancellation and runtime error close the handle and stop later turns.
- [ ] Recovery restores the checkpoint and validates any rotated binding.
- [ ] Unprofiled cells preserve current behavior.
- [ ] CLI code has no adapter module or provider handle.

## Test plan

- Success: two-turn profiled cell with fake environment, LLM, and operation. Assert exact lifecycle order.
- Invalid input: stale resolved profile and binding mismatch.
- Runtime failure: open, acquire, effect, checkpoint, close, and cleanup failures.
- Boundary and security: weak evidence prevents the first model/tool call; separate cells get distinct bindings.
- Deterministic capability: conformance adapter, resolver, policy, clocks, IDs, LLM, operations, and cancellation.
- JSONL and exit status: lifecycle failure produces one valid error case and exit 1; unknown profile remains exit 64.

## Documentation

Update Jidoka sequence and environment guides and the CLI one-session-per-cell description. Explain retention and cleanup by terminal state.

## Non-goals

Do not add a concrete backend. Do not expose raw handles. Do not pool environments across cells. Do not add result evidence fields in the CLI schema yet.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.3.5` — Persist portable execution bindings through recovery and fork
- `jido_cli-tqg.3.6` — Add data-only execution-profile selection and precedence
- `jido_cli-tqg.2.4` — Cancel headless sequences through public Jidoka handles

Features unlocked by this story:

- Confirmed enforcement fields in case results
- Constrained coding tools
- Security-aware run limits

## Commit plan

Create exactly two focused commits because the repositories have separate histories. First create one `jidoka` commit such as `feat(jidoka): attach constrained environments to cells (jido_cli-tqg.3.7)`. Then create one `jido_cli` commit such as `feat(cli): integrate attach constrained environments to cells (jido_cli-tqg.3.7)`. Do not include another backlog feature in either commit.

```sh
mix test test/jidoka/execution_environment/session_sequence_test.exs test/jidoka/session_sequence_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jido_cli
mix test test/jido_cli/cli/automation/engine/jidoka_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/automation_test.exs
mix quality
mix test --cover

```
